title: Precept Seven - Non-Elevating One's Self and Blaming Others
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up Precepts Six and Seven, not disparaging others and being humble, as two sides of one coin rooted in comparison and ranking. Nomon draws on a yoga class where the teacher says not to look around, Paul Warrick's advice to see oneself as neither better, worse, nor the same as others, and a student's remark that "it's difficult when I want." Norman Fischer's advice to new priests (be humble, try to help, see everyone as Buddha) and poems by David Budbill and Derek Walcott join a story of silent-retreat judgments that vanish when the person finally speaks. The session closes with a breakout exercise on the question "What makes you do it?"
